ruling.recommended_action: Send to RydeHELP human review as a safety case: check any speed/braking/telematics data for trip 08:36–08:51 NUS→Raffles Place, review the driver's post-trip statement (F6) under the code of conduct for abuse, and give the rider the reporting route (995 if medical help is needed / driver's commercial motor insurance for a claim). No fare adjustment on the current record (fixed RydeX fare, no routes deviating: F1, F2).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider-filed safety case: the rider alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder throughout the trip, and was scared [F1][F2]. Under SAFE-2 an allegation of dangerous driving means no automatic ruling and referral to a person; the trace confirms SAFE-1 screening applies and only escalate is available [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Reading the whole record for the safety screen: the chat itself is only pickup logistics — rider names her location and clothing, driver gives ETA and car [F3][F4], and the chat is complete and timestamped [F5], so nothing threatening there [SAFE-1]. The driver's post-trip statement, however, calls the rider "stupid" and hostilely blames her for being on the phone [F6]; hostile language aimed at the other party is abuse under the code of conduct, so my screen is at least "suspected" and the statement is put before the reviewer rather than weighed as a factual account [F6][SAFE-1]. This abusive sentence is not by itself a threat of violence, so the case is "suspected", not "confirmed".

The fare itself raises no independent claim: the distance actually driven (10.5 km) is shorter than the optimal route (10.6 km) and the duration (15.9 min) is below the estimate (16.5 min), so there is no off-route segment and no RD-2 mileage refund to compute [F1][F2][RD-2]; the RydeX fare is a fixed quote unaffected by these figures [RD-1][NS-7]. The alleged driving conduct is exactly what the record cannot test: there is no telematics, speed or lane-use fact, so the element the safety screen needs (whether the driving was dangerous) is missing rather than undetermined in the parties' favour [F6][SAFE-2]. Both profiles are long-standing with clean records [F7][F8], and profile facts never decide a case on their own, so they cannot make the safety allegation stand or fall [F7][F8][RD-6].

Because the safety screen is suspected and the evidence is insufficient to settle the dangerous-driving element, I do not rule on the substance; the case goes to a human reviewer with the facts above, and no amount is computed [SAFE-1][SAFE-2][NS-7].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety incident (dangerous-driving allegation) with no telematics record and abusive language in the driver's statement; human review required (SAFE-1, SAFE-2).

rejected_claims.reason: No claim survived in the rider's brief (advocate unavailable, judge-only ablation; requested no_action), so there is nothing to uphold: the complaint's dangerous-driving allegation is not settled by any record — no telematics/speed/braking fact exists (F1, F2 only give distance and duration), and the trace marks the case as a SAFE-1 safety incident requiring escalation rather than an automatic ruling [F1][F2][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The driver's brief also requested no_action with no surviving claim, and it rests on the driver's own account, which the record does not corroborate: his statement calls the rider 'stupid' (F6) and profiles are clean but cannot decide a case alone (F7, F8). A no_action outcome is unavailable here because the safety screen is suspected and the driving behaviour is unmeasured [F6][SAFE-1][SAFE-2][RD-6].

ruling.evidence_gap: No telematics or driving-behaviour record: the case has GPS distance/duration facts (F1, F2) and chat facts (F3–F6) but nothing on speed, braking, or lane/shoulder use — the record cannot settle whether the alleged speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking occurred.
